title: Spec Redd's band in Ottumwa
summary: He names the Redd brothers, bassist Francis Bates, trumpeter Leonard Chadwick and altoist Raymond Fields, a serious, sober band.

story.theme_name: Who was in the band: naming sidemen and personnel
story.community_name: Who played in the band: reciting personnel

blocks.x: And so I stayed there with Spec and the other guys that was there was Spec's brother, John. He played tenor. And he had another young brother who was Johnny.
Oh.
Little Johnny Redd.
Well, what did he do? That name is familiar to me, Little Johnny Redd.
Well, he changed his name. He went to California later and he was known as Yarlanda -- something from Redd. Colapanda, that's what it was. He changed it to Colapanda. And he --
(Inaudible.)
You figure just...
Turban on, if you saw him, you'd swear he was from the Indies somewhere.
No kidding?
He looked just like one, you see.
Is that right?
Yeah.
So what did he do? Sing?
No, played piano, and organ. He's playing now, I guess, somewhere.
Both the brothers played good piano.
Oh, yes. Well, Little Red, he would imitate everybody, too, just like his older brother.
Fancy that.
And he was very, very young. He was going to school, see.
Is that right?
And for his age, he was a genius.
Fancy that. That's interesting, isn't it?
And there was myself, Spec Redd, Johnny, --
Who was the bass player?
Francis Bates.
Good bass player?
He was a good bass player. He's in Des Moines now.
Is he?
And he's playing with the Dixieland Band.
Oh.
And also working at the airport.
Oh.
And Leonard Chadwick was the trumpet
player.
Oh, trumpet --
Trumpet and also fluegelhorn.
Oh, that was unusual in those days, wasn't it?
He's in this band here, with the Blue Devils.
Oh, Walter Paige?
Yeah, he played with them.
Oh.
I had this picture here I wanted to show you.
Oh, yeah.
I'll show it to you after awhile.
Okay.
But he was playing trumpet. And --
So there were good musicians in the band.
Oh, yes, very good musicians. And my buddy, he played alto.
Who was your buddy? Now I put you on the spot.
You got me on the spot again.
Yeah.
Raymond Fields.
Oh. He played alto?
He played alto and clarinet. He could play tenor, either one.
Oh, talented.
He was very talented.
He became a buddy of yours after you joined the band.
Right, right. We roomed together. We had the whole attic upstairs.
That's funny. So now, these guys were serious about their music.
Oh, yes, very much so.
They weren't heavy drinkers.
Oh, no, no, no. Everybody drank alike in this band. Nobody got drunk or nothing like that.
Yeah. So that satisfied you.
